Kuvitus: huoneen vaalea seinä, jossa sin: Illustration: a pale wall in a room, with a blue balloon staying stuck to the wall without tape, its string hanging down. On the left a plastic comb lies on a table, and small bits of paper rise from the table towards it.
Kaavakuva, ei mittakaavassa, kaksi panee: Schematic figure, not to scale, two panels. On the left before rubbing: the balloon and the wool cloth each have four positive and four negative charges, so each is neutral, Q = 0. On the right after rubbing: three electrons have moved from the wool to the balloon, shown by a blue arrow from the wool to the balloon. The balloon has four positive and seven negative charges, Q = −3e, and the wool has four positive and one negative charge, Q = +3e. The sum of the charges is still zero.

Schematic figure, not to scale, two panels. On the left a conductor: a negatively charged plastic rod is on the left of a metal sphere at the end of an insulating rod. The free electrons of the sphere have moved farther from the rod, so the surface of the sphere facing the rod has three positive charges and the opposite surface three negative charges; the sphere as a whole is neutral. A red force arrow points from the sphere towards the rod. On the right an insulator: a negatively charged balloon next to a wall. The charges in the molecules of the wall have shifted slightly so that the positive end of each molecule is towards the balloon. A red force arrow points from the balloon towards the wall.

Schematic figure, not to scale, two panels. On the left a positive point charge with eight radial field lines around it, arrows pointing away from the charge. On the right a negative point charge whose field line arrows point towards the charge. On the right of each there is a small positive test charge, and a red force arrow points in the direction of the field line: away from the positive charge and towards the negative charge. The field lines are green and the force arrow red. The lines are close together near the charge and spread out farther away.
Kaavakuva, ei mittakaavassa. Ylhäällä sa: Schematic figure, not to scale. At the top charges of the same sign q1 and q2, both positive: the force F21 on the charge q1 points to the left, away from q2, and the force F12 on the charge q2 to the right, away from q1, so the charges repel each other. At the bottom charges of opposite signs, q1 positive and q2 negative: the forces point towards each other, so the charges attract each other. All four force arrows are equally long. At the very bottom the distance r between the centres of the charges.
samanmerkkiset varaukset hylkivät: charges of the same sign repel
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: kahden pistevarau: Graph to scale: the force F between two point charges, q1 = q2 = 20 nC, in millinewtons as a function of the distance r in centimetres. The curve falls steeply. At a distance of 3 cm the force is 4.0 mN, at twice the distance, 6 cm, a quarter, that is 1.0 mN, at three times, 9 cm, a ninth, that is 0.44 mN, and at four times, 12 cm, a sixteenth, that is 0.25 mN. F, F/4, F/9 and F/16 are marked next to the points.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: kahden samanlaise: Graph to scale: the force F between two identical, equally charged small spheres in millinewtons as a function of the distance r between the centres of the spheres in centimetres, grid spacing 1 cm and 1 mN. The points calculated by the model are (3.0 cm; 8.99 mN), (4.0 cm; 5.06 mN), (5.0 cm; 3.24 mN), (6.0 cm; 2.25 mN) and (9.0 cm; 1.00 mN), and a falling curve passes through them.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: kahden varauspari: Graph to scale: the force F between two pairs of charges, A and B, in millinewtons as a function of the distance r between the centres of the spheres in centimetres, grid spacing 1 cm and 1 mN. The blue curve A starts at a distance of 3 cm and the red curve B at 4.4 cm; both fall as the distance grows, and curve B is above curve A all the way.
